title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr lightweight delayed matrix type R designed datasets large fit comfortably memory. Rather loading entire matrix , delarr keeps data disk (external storage) streams analysis pipeline manageable chunks. package keeps surface area deliberately small—one S3 class plus handful verbs—still supporting fused transformations, streaming reductions, pluggable backends. Operations lazy: build pipeline work executes call collect(). lets chain multiple transformations without intermediate allocations. vignette walks essentials: creating delayed arrays, building lazy pipelines, streaming HDF5 files, writing custom backends storage formats.

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr active development. Install latest development version cloning repository loading pkgload devtools: installed, load package:
code: # install.packages("pkgload") pkgload::load_all("/path/to/delarr") library(delarr)

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: core constructor delarr() wraps existing matrix (seed backend). transformation verbs—d_map(), d_center(), d_scale(), etc.—return new delarr without actually computing anything. operations recorded fused together, executed single pass call collect(). lazy evaluation two major benefits: Memory efficiency: Intermediate results never materialised. chain ten transformations uses memory one. Streaming: backed -disk storage, data flows pipeline chunks, can process datasets larger RAM. pipeline : d_center(dim = "rows") — subtracts row’s mean (operates across columns within row) d_map(~ .x * 0.5) — multiplies every element 0.5 (elementwise, row/column orientation) d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows") — computes mean row, collapsing single column
code: set.seed(1) mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), 5, 4) arr <- delarr(mat)  result <- arr |>   d_center(dim = "rows", na.rm = FALSE) |>   d_map(~ .x * 0.5) |>   d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows") |>   collect()  result #> [1] -1.561251e-17  6.938894e-18  0.000000e+00  1.387779e-17  0.000000e+00

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: Binary operations (d_map2() arithmetic operators) remain lazy support broadcasting scalars row/column vectors. add vector matrix, delarr automatically determines whether broadcast across rows columns based vector length. makes common operations like subtracting row means scaling column standard deviations simple memory-efficient—bias/scale vectors applied --fly chunk streams .
code: row_bias <- rnorm(nrow(mat))  delarr(mat) |>   (`+`)(row_bias) |>   (`*`)(1.5) |>   d_reduce(mean, dim = "cols") |>   collect(chunk_size = 2) #> [1] 0.3157507 0.3245493 0.1790303 0.8111963

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: HDF5 popular format storing large numerical arrays disk. delarr_hdf5() function creates delayed array backed HDF5 dataset, opening file collect() executes closing immediately . write results back disk without loading full matrix memory, pair pipeline hdf5_writer(). creates streaming sink receives data chunk--chunk. compression parameter controls gzip compression level (0-9, 4 good default balance speed size).

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: real power delarr comes pluggable backend system. storage layer—databases, cloud storage, memory-mapped files, custom binary formats—can become delarr backend implementing simple contract: Dimensions: Know total number rows columns Pull function: Given row column indices, return corresponding submatrix delarr_seed() function wraps two pieces seed object delarr() understands. pull function called lazily collect(), receiving indices needed current chunk.

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr provides focused set transformation verbs: - d_map() / d_map2(): Elementwise transformations using formula function syntax - d_center() / d_scale() / d_zscore(): Common preprocessing operations row column orientation - d_detrend(): Remove linear trends rows columns - d_where(): Masked updates—apply changes condition holds - d_reduce(): Row-wise column-wise reductions (sum, mean, min, max, custom functions) verbs return new delarr, can chain freely. operations fuse together execute single streaming pass.

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr uses several strategies minimise memory usage maximise throughput: Operation fusion. chain multiple transformations, delarr doesn’t create intermediate matrices. pipeline like d_center() |> d_map(~ .x * 2) |> d_scale() records three operations executes single pass. element centred, scaled, transformed together moving next chunk. Chunked streaming. Data flows pipeline column chunks (control size via chunk_size collect()). one chunk lives memory time, 10 GB matrix can processed just hundred megabytes RAM. Lazy file access. -disk backends like delarr_hdf5() delarr_mmap() open files collect() read columns needed current chunk. file handle closed immediately , avoiding resource leaks. Minimal dispatch overhead. delarr uses simple S3 classes closures rather S4 machinery. core execution loop tight column chunks direct function calls—method lookup per element. Streaming reductions. Operations like d_reduce(mean, dim = "cols") compute running accumulators chunks flow , never materialising full matrix. final result requires O(ncol) O(nrow) memory, O(nrow × ncol).

title: Getting Started with delarr
text: delarr good fit : data larger available RAM need apply pipeline many datasets want streaming /O without writing explicit chunking loops prefer simple, pipe-friendly API S4 complexity sparse matrices, GPU acceleration, parallel distributed computing, consider specialised packages. delarr focuses one thing well: efficient lazy operations dense, --core matrices.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: delarr provides lightweight delayed matrix type R tidy-friendly API. keeps surface area small—one S3 class plus handful verbs—offering fused elementwise transforms, reductions, streaming materialisation column chunks. Column blocks can also streamed straight disk via bundled HDF5 writer.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: package active development. Clone repository use pkgload::load_all() devtools::install() experiment API.
code: # install.packages("pkgload") pkgload::load_all(".")

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
code: library(delarr)  mat <- matrix(rnorm(20), 5, 4) arr <- delarr(mat)  # Lazy pipeline out <- arr |>   d_center(dim = "rows", na.rm = TRUE) |>   d_map(~ .x * 0.5) |>   d_reduce(mean, dim = "rows")  collect(out)

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
code: # assume `X` lives inside an HDF5 file lzy <- delarr_hdf5("input.h5", "X")  # Apply a transformation lazily and stream the result into a new dataset # (dim(lzy)[2] supplies the total column count for the writer) lzy |>   d_zscore(dim = "cols") |>   collect(into = hdf5_writer(     path = "output.h5",     dataset = "X_zscore",     ncol = dim(lzy)[2],     chunk = c(128L, 4096L)   ))

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: delarr_mem() wraps -memory matrix. delarr_hdf5() exposes dataset hdf5r. delarr_backend() lets create seed (rows, cols) -> matrix pull function. hdf5_writer() pairs collect(= ...) stream results back disk without materialising full matrix memory (supply ncol size destination dataset front). Additional backends (e.g., mmap) can layered supplying compatible pull function; extra dependencies ship core package.

title: Lazy Delayed Arrays with Fused Execution
text: d_map()/d_map2() elementwise transformations. d_center()/d_scale()/d_zscore()/d_detrend() common preprocessing, optional na.rm handling. d_reduce() row-wise column-wise reductions, streaming na.rm support sum/mean/min/max. d_where() masked updates, optionally replacing masked entries via fill argument. collect() realise data (streamed chunks), optionally writing disk hdf5_writer(), block_apply() chunk-wise computation. verbs return another delarr, pipelines stay lazy collect() materialises result.
